newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE VICTORY REVIVES TITLE HOPES.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-VILLENEUVE VICTORY REVIVES TITLE HOPES.

text.p: Jacques Villeneuve revived his challenge for the world drivers' championship with a dramatic victory in the British Grand prix on Sunday.
The Canadian regained the lead during the closing laps after mechanical problems had wrecked the hopes of both German Michael Schumacher and Mika Hakkinen of Finland.
Villeneuve, driving a Williams, repeated his win in last year's race for his fourth victory of the season and eighth of his career.
It was also the 100th victory of the Williams team and came on the same Silverstone circuit where they won their first thanks to Swiss Clay Regazzoni in 1979.
The victory was the sixth by the Williams team in the last seven British Grands Prix and the seventh in succession by a Renault-powered car.
Frenchman Jean Alesi finished second in a Benetton ahead of his young Austrian team mate Alexander Wurz, driving in only his third Grand Prix.
Briton David Coulthard was fourth in a McLaren ahead of 21-year-old German Ralf Schumacher in a Jordan and Briton Damon Hill in an Arrows.
For World Champion Hill, it was his first point in a year of tribulation and provided some solace at the end of a weekend overshadowed by rumours about his future.

Championship leader Michael Schumacher looked certain to claim another win until he was forced to retire with a mechanical problem after 37 laps. But he remains on top with 47 points to Villeneuve's 43.

Hakkinen also led the race but was forced out by a blown engine which allowed villeneuve, who had led in the early laps, to make up for a near-disastrous 33.6 second pit stop in the early stages and claim victory.
